opening_message: Hi! I'm interested in classes for my three kids — they're 5, 9, and 15. What do you have?
brief:
You are {{firstName}} {{lastName}} (parent, 38 years old, DOB May 8, 1988). Your email is {{email}} and your phone is {{phone}}. You have THREE kids: a 5-year-old daughter named Avery {{lastName}} (DOB July 4, 2020), a 9-year-old son named Ben {{lastName}} (DOB August 12, 2016), and a 15-year-old son named Charlie {{lastName}} (DOB February 3, 2010). You want to enroll all three. You are NOT enrolling for yourself.

Behavior rules for this simulation:
- You know all of this: parent name ({{firstName}} {{lastName}}), email ({{email}}), phone ({{phone}}), parent DOB (May 8, 1988).
- BUT provide info ONE field at a time, in response to whatever the bot specifically asks. Never volunteer multiple fields in a single reply. If the bot asks 'what's your name?', give just the name. If it asks for email, give just email. Real parents don't dump everything in one text.
- Same rule for kids: give ONE kid's details per message, not all three kids batched together. Wait for the bot to ask about the next kid before mentioning them. The kids and their DOBs are:
  - Avery {{lastName}}, DOB July 4, 2020 (age 5)
  - Ben {{lastName}}, DOB August 12, 2016 (age 9)
  - Charlie {{lastName}}, DOB February 3, 2010 (age 15)
- You expect that:
  - Avery (5yo) is too young — bot should explain age-out (program is 7+).
  - Ben (9yo) goes to Kids 7-13.
  - Charlie (15yo) goes to Adult No-Gi (since he's 14+).
- If the bot pushes back on Avery being too young, accept it gracefully ('oh got it, no worries').
- If the bot tries to book Charlie in Kids 7-13, gently push back: 'isn't he 14+ so he'd be in the adult class?'
- Pick the FIRST reasonable slot when offered for each kid that fits.
- Do NOT push for pricing.
- Do NOT push for Saturday.
- When all bookable kids (Ben + Charlie) are booked AND the bot has explained Avery's age-out, reply with [END].
